skill.name: UTM Tracking and Campaign Tracking
skill.description: Adding UTM parameters to URLs to track marketing campaign effectiveness across channels, including UTM builder, attribution models, analytics integration, and campaign reporting.

generated_query: I’m launching a new product next month and will be promoting it through email newsletters, Facebook ads, and a Google Ads campaign. I need to create trackable links for each channel so I can see which source drives the most conversions. Could you help me build the URLs with the correct UTM parameters? For the email, the link should point to my product page (https://example.com/product) with source as “newsletter,” medium as “email,” and campaign name “product-launch-2025.” For Facebook ads, source “facebook,” medium “cpc,” campaign same name, and content “hero-image-ad.” For Google Ads, source “google,” medium “cpc,” campaign name, and include the term “buy-now.” Also, I’d like a simple spreadsheet or table that lists each final URL and the parameters used, so I can verify them before launching. After the campaign runs, I want to be able to pull a report showing clicks and conversions per source—can you advise on how to set that up in Google Analytics or a similar tool?

edit_instructions.rationale: Removing the paid search URL builder prevents generating the Google Ads link with the required 'buy-now' term parameter, making the skill unable to fulfill the user's request.
Replaces the medium assignment with a source-dependent mapping that forces Facebook ads to use 'social_paid' instead of the user-specified 'cpc', breaking the Facebook tracking URL.
Adds a condition to skip the content parameter for Facebook source, so the 'hero-image-ad' content is omitted from the Facebook URL.
Changed email campaign URL builder to use source 'email' instead of 'newsletter', causing the generated URL to have wrong UTM parameter for the user's email newsletter link.
Changed social media URL builder to use medium 'organic_social' instead of 'cpc', making the Facebook ad URL fail the user's required medium.

edit_instructions.rationale: Removes the dedicated email UTM builder, so the skill cannot generate the required email tracking links with correct source and medium.
Removes the social media URL builder, making the skill unable to produce Facebook ad links with the correct source, medium, and content parameter.
Removes the paid search URL builder, so the skill cannot generate Google Ads links with the required term parameter.
Deleting the buildURL method removes the core functionality to generate trackable URLs, making the skill unable to create the specific campaign links requested by the user.
The buildEmailURL method sets utm_source to 'email' instead of 'newsletter', so the email link would have incorrect tracking source, breaking the user's requirement for source='newsletter'.
Changes the social URL builder to use 'display' instead of 'cpc', so the Facebook ad link will have the wrong medium parameter.
Replaces the keyword parameter in the paid search builder with an empty string, so the Google Ads link will not include the required 'buy-now' term.
Removing the required parameter checks weakens the validation, allowing URLs to be built without mandatory UTM parameters, which the user query specifically needs to track conversions correctly.
